newsitem.title: USA: Delta's Worth says not interviewing for top job.
newsitem.headline: Delta's Worth says not interviewing for top job.

text.p: Maurice Worth, who was named acting chief executive officer of Delta Air Lines Inc on Thursday, said he is not interviewing for the job of permanent CEO.
"I have not been interviewed for the job and I am doing the job that I have been assigned to do," Worth said.

"I've been part of the vision and part of the strategy and I have been asked to continue to take the company forward during this transition period and I'm concentrating my efforts on that," Worth said.
Earlier on Thursday, Delta tapped Worth, who is currently the airline's executive vice president of customer service and acting chief operating officer, to serve as acting CEO.
Delta also named Mary Johnston Evans, a member of Delta's board since 1983, as acting non-executive chairman.
The two acting officers will serve after the July 31 retirement of current Chairman Ronald Allen.
Allen's departure after 34 years with Delta surprised industry experts, who suggested at the time that his resignation followed a rift with the board about the company's strategic focus.
Worth will oversee the airline's daily operations worldwide, while Evans will handle board issues until a permanent chairman is named.
Once Delta names a permanent chief executive, Worth said he hopes to play "an active role at Delta."
"I've committed 36 years to the company and have been a part of the success and part of the Delta people ... I hope I can take an active role going forward.
Throughout his tenure at Delta, Worth has worked in operations, station management, personnel and executive management.

The company declined to comment on the timeframe for its executive search or to discuss how many candidates have been interviewed. At a press conference in Atlanta, Evans said the company continues to look at candidates both inside and outside the airline industry.
Evans said Delta is not looking to dramatically change direction, but the airline could be open to an executive that brings a fresh perspective to the industry.
Delta is looking for "someone who recognizes the strengths that Delta has now and (can) help them to grow. Maybe someone who has a new look at the industry. We're looking inside and

"There's so many things at Delta (that) don't need changing, just reinforcing. We're proud of what we have done and what we have accomplished. We just need to keep doing more of the same," Evans said.
"We can always learn from outside, but I think we think the direction we're going is just right," Evans said.
